feedback:
Written before this candidate races. It changes only the sensor x positions, widening the span from ±0.03 m to ±0.04 m (20 mm spacing), and keeps base_speed 1.3, kp 5.0, ki 0.05, kd 0.5 and last_direction. The change follows iteration 1, where widening the span from ±0.02 m to ±0.03 m cut line-loss events from about 2.0 to 1.0 to 1.95 per run depending on track, while kp, kd and speed stayed fixed. Iteration 1 max_error was 0.060 to 0.066 m on all tracks, so the failure chain is still line loss followed by drift past the 0.06 m limit. The candidate is valid: all values are inside the contract ranges, the weights keep the signal bounded by 1, and the sensors at ±0.04 m can still see tape at offsets of about 0.02 m, which matches the limit. It is a single, diagnosed change with a clear comparison to the best raced design (193.19), so it is worth racing for per-step telemetry.

What to do next, depending on the race: (a) If line_loss_events is still above about 0.5 per run, the outer sensors are not the limit. Keep the ±0.04 span, and check whether the loss is concentrated on one track. (b) If line_loss_events is near 0 but max_error is still at or above 0.06 m with off-track ends, raise kp toward 6.0, since the correction is too weak. (c) If the robot finishes and line loss is near 0, check completion_time. If it is above 3 s, raise base_speed toward 1.5. Watch steering_oscillation: if it rises sharply with the wider span or higher kp, raise kd toward 0.7 before changing anything else.
requested_changes: If line_loss_events stays above about 0.5 per run with the ±0.04 m span: keep base_speed at 1.3 and check which track still loses the line, because iteration 1 showed 1.0 to 1.95 events per run with the ±0.03 m span.

If line_loss_events is near 0 but the robot still ends off track with max_error at or above 0.06 m: raise controller.kp from 5.0 to about 6.0, since the failures in iterations 0 and 1 came from drift past the limit rather than from line loss alone.

If the robot finishes with line_loss_events near 0 but completion_time is above 3 s: raise controller.base_speed toward 1.5. If steering_oscillation rises sharply, raise controller.kd toward 0.7 instead of changing speed.
